newsitem.title: GERMANY: Veba outperforms after upbeat first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Veba outperforms after upbeat first quarter.

text.p: German energy and telecommunications group Veba AG said on Tuesday it expected to increase its profits this year after an unexpectedly good first quarter and amid continued efforts to cut costs.
In a statement which sent its share price surging, Veba reported a seven percent rise in first quarter net profit to 486 million marks ($281 million) and an eight percent increase in sales.

Growth was driven by "significant" earnings and sales advances in its oil business and its trading, transport and services division, although the chemical sector business was hampered by high raw materials costs, Veba said.
Utilities analysts applauded the figures but adopted a wait-and-see attitude on whether the earnings growth would continue for the full year.

Roland Pitz, utilities analyst at Bayerische Hypo-Bank in Munich, said: "The performance was better than I expected. From the structural side, the performance was less surprising. We saw a good performance in the oil sector, although the chemical sector was weaker in the first quarter."

"We are keeping our earnings outlook for Veba unchanged at 5.47 marks per share for 1997 and 5.81 for 1998. We are also keeping our recommendation for the share at "market performer", although we expect the share to be an "outperformer" in the short-term because it has underperformed of late," said Pitz.
Veba's sales in the first quarter rose 7.8 percent to 19.624 billion marks, with oil sales showing the biggest advance to rise 19.1 percent to 4.925 billion marks.
In the chemicals sector, sales dropped by 1.6 percent to 2.6 billion marks.
Peter Antes, utilities analyst at Bayerische Vereinsbank, said the results were a "positive surprise".
"The dollar certainly played a role in boosting Veba's oil business. But in the whole group there were positive and negative influences from the dollar," said Antes.

Not everyone was as enthusiastic about the outlook for the group. Robert Willis, German equities analyst at Schroder Securities in London, felt that the positive effects of the dollar's appreciation meant earnings growth was overstated.
"We are maintaining our full-year estimate for earnings at six percent and we are keeping Veba on "sell", which is the recommendation we have had for a year now."
"We think it is overvalued, overdiversified and overambitious in too many areas," said Willis.

"If you look carefully at these figures they are not so impressive. The price of oil is up 28 percent in deutschemark terms on a year ago, which is a major contribution to earnings growth," said Willis.

Antes said that the dollar had both negative and positive effects. "The chemical sector suffered from the higher dollar because of increased raw materials costs, for example. Veba said that the dollar doesn't play a major overall role in the whole group," said Antes.

"The electricity sector did better than we expected, but this was mainly because Veba had no nuclear plant shutdowns during the year and because it was able to import electricity from Sweden," said Willis.
"The chemical sector did worse than expected, but this was offset by the better oil performance," said Willis.
Veba said it expected to increase its profits this year after an unexpectedly good first quarter and amid continued efforts to cut costs.
The utility group's shares surged on the news and hit highs of 94.02 marks in bourse trade on Tuesday.

By the end of electronic trade on the IBIS DAX index, Veba was up 2.72 marks, or 3.02 percent, at 92.92 marks, while the overall IBIS DAX index ended down 17.17 points, or 0.48 percent, at 3,548.52 points.
--Clifford Coonan, Frankfurt Newsroom +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.727 German Marks)
